newsitem.title: UK: UK reforms put PFI projects at risk - Conservatives.
newsitem.headline: UK reforms put PFI projects at risk - Conservatives.

text.p: Britain's opposition Conservative Party on Monday condemned reforms to the Private Finance Initiative announced earlier on Monday by the Labour government as "rearranging the deckchairs".
David Heathcoat-Amory, newly appointed shadow Chief Secretary to the Treasury, said the Labour Party's actions since taking office "have put the PFI on hold and PFI projects at risk".
The government announced it was to set up a Treasury Private Finance Taskforce, which would assess potential PFI projects for their commercial viability before procurement begins.

Heathcoat-Amory said in a statement: "The Government...plans to bring the PFI under Treasury control and increase public sector involvement. Yet in opposition they alleged that the PFI was stifled by bureaucracy and red tape."

"Today's announcement is yet another example of Labour behaving in government as if they were still in opposition -- rearranging the deckchairs without making any substantive improvement at all," he added.

He said that Labour had sacked the chairman of the Private Finance Panel shortly after taking office. There would now be further delay,, while it considered who to appoint as head of the new Taskforce.
